Fit models with different numbers of classes and collect their criteria and diagnostics for comparison

Source: R/enumeration.R
enumerate_classes.Rd

enumerate_classes() fits every candidate in a grid of class counts (and, for continuous indicators, covariance structures) and collects their information criteria, classification quality and estimation diagnostics in one object. It covers latent profile, latent class and latent transition models, single-level or two-level, and the additive, dispersion and additive-dispersion families of multilpa(). The fitted candidates stay in the result (see Value).

Information criteria summarise relative support; entropy and average posteriors describe classification certainty within each candidate. Neither picks a solution: also check that the best likelihood was replicated across starts, that no estimate sits at a bound, and that an added class brings interpretable differences in the response patterns. More profiles can stand in for covariances a diagonal structure cannot hold, so compare class counts alongside plausible structures. The grid is the analyst's: when every criterion is lowest at its edge, extend it.

Usage

enumerate_classes(
  data,
  vars,
  id,
  n_profiles = 1:4,
  n_group_classes = 1:3,
  model = "basic",
  seed = NULL,
  family = "profiles",
  between_variance = c("varying", "equal"),
  time = NULL,
  ...,
  cores = 1L,
  type = NULL,
  verbose = cores > 1L
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per observation: the indicators, the group identifier and, when used, the occasion column and covariates. Use the same rows and scale for every candidate.

vars

Names of the indicator columns.

id

The column identifying the groups the rows are nested in. NULL enumerates single-level models, with a message; enumerate_lpa() and enumerate_lca() do that directly.

n_profiles

Profile (class) counts to try (default 1:4; 2:4 for transition models, which need at least two profiles).

n_group_classes

Group-class counts to try (default 1:3; default 1 with time, and only 1 with id = NULL). Every count is crossed with every value of n_profiles. A candidate with one profile and more than one group class is not identified: it is recorded as failed, with the reason in the error column.

model

The covariance structures of the continuous indicators to fit at every combination of class counts:

  • "basic" (default for profile models): four structures. "EEI": the profiles share their variances and the indicators are uncorrelated within a profile. "VVI": each profile has its own variances, still uncorrelated. "EEE": the profiles share one covariance matrix. "VVV": each profile has its own covariance matrix.

  • "all": all fourteen structures of mclust.

  • One or more of the codes "EII", "VII", "EEI", "VEI", "EVI", "VVI", "EEE", "VEE", "EVE", "VVE", "EEV", "VEV", "EVV", "VVV": those structures only. The three letters are the volume, shape and orientation, each equal (E) or varying (V) across profiles, with I for a spherical shape or no covariances; multilpa() explains them.

  • NULL: no structure is crossed, and every candidate has the structure multilpa() fits by default ("VVI"). This is the default with time.

With time, only codes and NULL are accepted ("basic" and "all" are not). With one continuous indicator, codes that coincide are fitted once. With no continuous indicator there is no structure to cross, and an explicit model is an error. Giving variance_model, covariance_model, volume, shape or orientation in ... sets one structure for every candidate; model must then be left out.

seed

Optional integer seed, reproducing the starting values for the same data and controls.

family

Which model family to enumerate:

  • "profiles" (default): the profile model, over n_profiles, n_group_classes and model;

  • one or more of "additive", "dispersion" and "additive_dispersion": those group-class families of multilpa(), over family, n_group_classes and between_variance. They need id, refuse n_profiles, model and time, and return a latents_family_enumeration.

The cross-level families of multilpa() are not enumerated.

between_variance

For the group-class families only, the restrictions on the between-group variances to cross:

  • "varying": each group class has its own between-group variances;

  • "equal": all group classes share them.

The default, c("varying", "equal"), fits both. The dispersion family is fitted with "equal" only. Giving the argument with family = "profiles" is an error.

time

The occasion column. Enumerates latent transition models (lta()) over n_profiles and n_group_classes, every other lta() argument in ... held fixed; model, when given, crosses structures. Profile family only; returns a latents_transition_enumeration. NULL (default) enumerates profile or class models.

...

Further arguments of multilpa(), or of lta() with time, used for every candidate: typically n_starts, max_iter, missing ("error" or "fiml"), categorical, centering, scaling, drop_empty and boundary ("allow" or "exclude"). The group-class families take only n_starts, max_iter, tol and min_variance. A name that is not an argument of the fitting function is refused.

cores

Maximum number of parallel workers (default 1, serial). With seed, parallel and serial runs give the same result. On Windows, and on macOS with Apple's Accelerate BLAS, each worker is a separate R process, so memory grows with cores.

type

The kind of model, stated explicitly:

  • NULL (default): read from the other arguments. time gives transition models; otherwise the indicators named in categorical, ordinal and count decide between profile, class and mixed models;

  • "lpa": latent profile models. Every indicator is continuous; categorical, ordinal and count are refused;

  • "lca": latent class models. Every indicator is categorical, numeric codes included, as multilca() does (indicators in ordinal or count keep those distributions, and categorical adds to the set);

  • "lta": latent transition models. Needs time, and reads the measurement from categorical, as lta() does, without making numeric indicators categorical.

"lpa" and "lca" need time = NULL, and an explicit type needs family = "profiles".

verbose

TRUE reports progress with one message each when the candidates are prepared, when starts are screened, when they are fitted and when the grid is done; FALSE is silent. The default is TRUE when cores > 1 and FALSE otherwise. Not reported for the group-class families.

Value

An enumeration grid that keeps every fitted candidate. Its class depends on what was enumerated:

  • multilpa_enumeration: profile, class or mixed models (the default);

  • latents_transition_enumeration: transition models (with time);

  • latents_family_enumeration: group-class families (with family).

The print header names the resolved type (LPA, LCA, LTA, mixed or family).

On every grid, get_candidates() (also as.data.frame()) gives one row per candidate, named like "profiles3_groups2": with the structure appended, as in "profiles3_groups2_VVI", when several are crossed; with classes for profiles when every indicator is categorical; without the groups part on a single-level grid ("profiles3"); and by family on a family grid ("additive_groups2"). Its columns:

  • n_profiles, n_group_classes, model, log_likelihood and n_parameters;

  • the information criteria aic, kic, bic, sabic, caic, awe, icl and clc. On a profile or class grid each except aic and kic has two columns: _groups uses the number of groups as the sample size and _individual the number of rows. Lower is better. A transition or family grid has aic, bic (groups) and bic_individual;

  • profile_entropy and group_entropy (entropy on a transition or family grid): relative entropy between 0 and 1, higher meaning clearer classification;

  • on a profile or class grid, the average posterior probability of the assigned class (avepp_min, avepp_max, avepp_mean, and avepp_below, the number of classes under 0.8), with the same for group classes as group_avepp_*;

  • converged, boundary (an estimate at its bound) and n_best_replicated (the number of starts that reached the best log likelihood);

  • error: why a candidate could not be fitted. Such a candidate keeps its row, with NA values. A transition or family grid also has warnings, the warnings of each candidate.

Columns empty in every row are left out. The other accessors: get_best() gives the best candidate per criterion; get_tree() and plot_tree() how classes split; get_entropy(), get_avepp() and get_classification() the classification tables of every candidate; plot_criteria() the criteria; get_candidate() one fitted candidate; compare_models() candidates by name (a family grid is compared in its own candidates table). A profile or class grid also has get_deltas() and get_knees(), and a summary() that prints one screen of the evidence; a transition or family grid's summary() is its candidates table. No candidate is selected automatically.

Conditions

latents_bad_argument for an argument value or combination that is not accepted: a type that conflicts with time, family or the measurement arguments; model given with another structure argument, with no continuous indicator, or naming an unknown structure; n_profiles or model with a group-class family; between_variance with the profile family; more than one group class with id = NULL; a name in ... that the fitting function does not have. latents_bad_transition for a transition grid with fewer than two profiles. A candidate that fails for a reason of its own stays in the grid with its error. When every candidate fails for the same reason in the data or the arguments (a column that does not exist, for example), that error is raised instead: latents_bad_data, latents_bad_categorical, latents_missing_data, latents_bad_weights or latents_bad_argument. The candidates' warnings are raised once the grid is fitted. When a converged candidate fitted from two or more starts reached its best log likelihood from one of them only, a latents_single_start message names it once per grid. latents-conditions lists every condition.

See also

get_candidate(), bootstrap_lrt() to test one class count against the next, enumerate_regressions() for mixture regressions.

Examples

# Course sessions nested in students: numbers of session profiles and of
# student classes.
activity <- c("browse", "lectures")
candidates <- enumerate_classes(course_engagement, activity, id = "student",
                                n_profiles = 2:3, n_group_classes = 1:2,
                                model = "VVI", n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
#> 2 of 4 candidates reached their best log likelihood from one start only (profiles3_groups1, profiles3_groups2); refit those you consider with more starts.
candidates

# Latent transition models over each student's sequence of sessions:
moves <- enumerate_classes(course_engagement,
                           c(activity, "forum_read", "forum_post",
                             "attendance"),
                           id = "student", time = "sequence",
                           n_profiles = 2:3, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
get_candidates(moves)

# Latent class models, stated explicitly with `type`:
items <- c("time_with_friends", "on_social_media", "tv_video_games",
           "sports")
classes <- enumerate_classes(subset(student_esm, day <= 1), items,
                             id = "student", type = "lca",
                             n_profiles = 1:2, n_group_classes = 1,
                             n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
